newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher on exports, weather.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher on exports, weather.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly higher on bullish export data and persistent concerns about dry weather in western Kansas, traders said.
Dry wheat growing areas in western Kansas may receive scattered showers late this weekend or next week, but the long-term outlook for that area remains dry, meteorologists said.
"The market is at the point where it knows it's either 20 cents too high or 10 cents too cheap, and it will know which way to go after this weekend's weather," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said volumes were light late in the session as the market awaited private forecasts for weekend weather.

Traders cited USDA's weekly export sales report as another source of support. USDA said net combined old and new crop export sales during the week ended May 8 totaled 705,500 tonnes, exceeding expectations of 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Firm cash basis markets underpinned the nearby May contract, adding strength to the May/July spread.
KCBT wheat settled 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 13 cents higher, with May up 13 cents at $4.68. July was up 2-3/4 cents at $4.19.
